concerns.text: T014 (evaluation) depends on T015b (route complexity metrics), but T015b depends on T007 (graph validation). T007 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) in Phase 2, yet T015b explicitly requires the graph from T007. If T007 runs in parallel with T006 (preprocess), T015b cannot start until T007 finishes. However, T014 also depends on T015b. The current ordering implies T014 can start after T006, but it actually requires T007 to complete first. This creates a hidden dependency chain: T006 -> T007 -> T015b -> T014. The [P] tag on T007 is misleading if it blocks downstream tasks in Phase 3.

T023a and T023b (Chi-squared scans) depend on T014 (evaluation), which already performs 'point-wise Chi-squared scans' and identifies the inflection point. This creates a circular or redundant dependency where the statistical analysis in Phase 4 depends on the same analysis already performed in Phase 3. The tasks should be re-ordered to either consolidate the Chi-squared logic into a single task or clearly separate the 'detection' (Phase 3) from the 'correction/validation' (Phase 4) to avoid implicit re-computation or ordering conflicts.

T028 (profiling lightweight model) depends on T012 (lightweight model). T030 (profiling baseline) depends on T013 (baseline). However, T030 also requires the baseline to run to completion to record 'timeout/infeasible' status. If the baseline fails to load (T013), T030 cannot proceed. The current ordering does not explicitly handle the case where T013 fails, potentially causing T030 to hang or crash. A dependency check or conditional task flow is needed to handle the 'inconclusive' status gracefully.

T007 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but depends on T004 (download) and produces output required by T015b (Phase 3). While T007 can run in parallel with T006 (preprocess), the [P] tag might mislead implementers into thinking it has no downstream dependencies. Clarify that T007 is parallel-safe with T006 but blocks T015b.
